title: Submit Your Questions: The Great Data Center Backlash
gist: WIRED is hosting a September 10, 2026 livestream AMA on 'the great data center backlash,' pairing its science/politics, climate/energy, DC politics, and AI-business reporters to address the topic as a cross-cutting political, business, and environmental issue ahead of the 2026 midterms.

themes.theme: Data center backlash framed as a major cross-beat story

insights.claim: WIRED is treating data center backlash as a significant enough cross-cutting political, business, and environmental issue to warrant a dedicated expert livestream AMA on September 10, 2026, rather than a single article.
insights.speaker: Tim Marchman
insights.so_what: A major outlet elevating this topic to panel-event status is itself a signal of the theme's growing salience for tracking policy and infrastructure risk through the 2026 midterms.
insights.quote: The infrastructure powering the AI industry is at the heart of heated discussions of politics, business, and the environment

insights.claim: The panel pairs WIRED's senior director of science, politics, and security (Tim Marchman) with its climate/energy reporter (Molly Taft), a DC political correspondent (Hugo Lowell), and its AI-business reporter (Maxwell Zeff), reflecting a view that the data center story spans energy, politics, and AI-business simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Tim Marchman
insights.so_what: The multi-beat panel composition indicates the outlet expects reader questions to cut across energy costs, political backlash, and AI industry economics rather than any single narrow angle.

insights.claim: The data center AMA follows previous WIRED livestreams on AI and work, the defense tech industry, and the future of electric vehicles, part of a recurring editorial series on major tech-economy inflection points.
insights.speaker: Tim Marchman
insights.so_what: Signals WIRED views data centers as belonging to the same tier of major structural tech-economy stories as defense tech and EVs, useful context for gauging how mainstream the topic has become.
